metadata.description: Xaaalera personal Claude Code skills, grouped by domain. marketplace.json is generated from plugins/<domain>/plugin.json; plugins/ and README.md are hand-edited.

plugins.name: cerberus
plugins.description: CERBERUS — the two-headed guard at the gate for a PUBLIC skills marketplace. A PostToolUse hook fires on every skill / reference / script / eval / manifest edit and reminds you to run BOTH heads before committing: cerberus:leak-check (outward — no real work identifier or secret escapes into the public marketplace) and cerberus:security-scan (inward — the eight-point consumer-safety checklist: prompt injection, exfiltration, secrets, dangerous commands, obfuscation, external fetches, credential access, privilege escalation, so nothing unsafe reaches whoever installs the skill). Both are agent judgment passes, no denylist by design — a list of the real names to catch would itself be the leak; the intelligence lives in the agent, not a regex.

plugins.name: cicero
plugins.description: CICERO — the house voice. The numbered communication rules under one governing readability rule (result first, plain words, recommend one option, push back with reasons, honesty about verification, stay in scope) ship as a force-for-plugin output style applied at the system-prompt level. Four floor rules are invariants; every other rule is a user-overridable default. 2.3.0 inverts the shape default: prose unless a trigger fires, with a checkable situation-to-shape map, a ban on two adjacent blocks sharing a shape, a measured device inventory in which bold is no longer load-bearing, and a bar-and-title heading. The honesty floor now forbids ending a turn on a promise — a turn ends DONE, BLOCKED, or CONTINUING-and-continuing — because asking an agent to narrate its progress is itself a documented cause of premature stopping. A SessionStart hook shows a banner with a worked example of the finding-tree notation and picks the conversation language; a UserPromptSubmit hook keeps the reply language current.

plugins.name: critique
plugins.description: Adversarial critique — the house method for red-teaming a design, spec, or plan with diverse independent lenses so a critique detects real defects instead of laundering a green stamp.

plugins.name: diagram
plugins.description: Architecture / flow diagram authoring — turn a spec or raw code into a readable, clickable D2→ELK diagram (classes with methods, objects, permission sets, relations) as a browsable HTML page under docs/diagrams/<name>/. Node contents come from an Atlas entity list that parallel Sextant reviewer agents harden to zero edits.

plugins.name: plan-gate
plugins.description: Spec+Plan+Branch gate — a PreToolUse hook that blocks Edit/Write to code unless you are off the base branch (default `main`) AND a plan exists for the work: a branch task-id (e.g. PROJ-1234) must match a plan filename, else any branch-new or uncommitted plan file suffices. docs/ is always writable so the spec/plan itself is never blocked. Opt-in per repo via .claude/plan-gate.config.json; bypass one edit with SKIP_PLAN_GATE=1.

plugins.name: review
plugins.description: Stack-agnostic pre-push review framework — eight reviewer agents (five on by default, plus skill, leak and security-scan for repos that publish skills), the /review orchestrator, and the secret-scan + attestation gate, all driven by a per-project .claude/review.config.json.

plugins.name: review-workflow
plugins.description: Workflow script for the pre-push review gate — dispatches the review plugin's lenses in parallel with a forced response schema, reconciles findings, recomputes each lens's score with the round-aware formula, and checks the eight gate criteria before the review command may attest. No skill; invoked directly by the review plugin's /review command.

plugins.name: salesforce
plugins.description: Personal Salesforce skills — Apex test authoring standard and salesforce-dx MCP usage.

plugins.name: scout
plugins.description: Passive skill that reads the compiled catalog to discover/recommend/install marketplace skills, surfaces declared side effects, and treats catalog text as untrusted data.

plugins.name: skillcraft
plugins.description: Skill quality & improvement — measuring whether a guide skill actually helps, diagnosing where it falls short, and improving it without regressions. Home for skill-improvement methods and metrics.

plugins.name: tests
plugins.description: Test standard as an installable plugin — the execution-tier split, the test contract, the axes a case space is derived from, factories, matchers and fakes, a JSON failure envelope, and the coverage and mutation gates. Ships a whole-tree audit agent and the config a repository states its own numbers in.
